steps.body: A record keeps every measurement, including repeats. Each measured ribbon needs one entry.
steps.narration: A record keeps every measurement, including repeats. Each measured ribbon needs one entry.

widget.prompt: Record the counts so far as tallies: 6 cm seen 3 times, 7 cm twice, 8 cm once.
widget.successFeedback: Three, two, one — every measurement remembered, repeats and all.
widget.partialFeedback: Match each tally group to how many times that measurement appeared — repeats each earn a mark.

predict.prompt: Your record drops the repeated 6s. What is lost?
predict.reveal: The value 6 survives, but its three-ness dies — and frequency is what the plot will need.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2g record.
invariants: A display and its data are the same information in two forms: every measurement appears exactly once, and counts survive the trip into stacks, rows, and bars for g2g record.
misconceptions: Reading a label as a count, dropping repeats while recording, or comparing categories by adding instead of finding the gap.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change to the data would the display be FORCED to show — and what change could it silently hide?

widget.prompt: Five ribbons measure 6, 8, 6, 7, and 6 cm. Which record keeps the same five results?

options.label: 6, 8, 6, 7, 8 cm
options.feedback: The last 6 was changed to 8, so this is different data.

options.label: 6, 8, 7, 7, 6 cm
options.feedback: One 6 was changed to 7, so this is different data.

options.label: 6, 6, 6, 7, 7 cm
options.feedback: The 8 was changed to 7, so this is different data.

options.label: 6, 8, 6, 7, 6 cm
options.feedback: Correct — all five results, including all three 6s, are present.

hints: Mark to mark is the length.

widget.prompt: Make tallies for a second record: 5 cm once, 6 cm three times, and 7 cm twice.
widget.successFeedback: One, three, two — the new tally keeps all six measurements, including repeats.
widget.partialFeedback: Give every repeated measurement its own tally in the matching length row.

widget.prompt: A ribbon in the group stretches from the 2 cm mark to the 11 cm mark. How long is it?

commonErrors.feedback: That read the end mark as the length — subtract where the ribbon starts.
Adding the two mark numbers does not give the length; subtract the start from the end.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Subtract the start mark from the end mark; the gap between them is the ribbon's length.

hints: Mark to mark is the length.

concept.body: Do not erase a repeated measurement. Two ribbons that both measure 4 cm still need two separate entries.
concept.narration: Do not erase a repeated measurement. Two ribbons that both measure 4 cm still need two separate entries.

widget.prompt: Four ribbons measure 4, 4, 6, and 7 cm. Which record keeps every result?

options.label: 4, 6, 7, 8 cm
options.feedback: One 4 is missing and an 8 was added.

options.label: 4, 4, 6, 7 cm
options.feedback: Correct — both 4s and the 6 and 7 are recorded.
